thesis: e.l.f. Beauty closed fiscal 2026 (ended 2026-03-31) with net sales +25% to $1.636B and a 35% Q4 (+$449.3M, beating $424.8M consensus), with all five brands growing and the newly acquired Rhode at ~$390M annualized sales growing ~80% y/y. The stock collapsed early in 2026, then rebounded ~47% through June and into July (pass1 shows +21.0% over 5 days to $73.49) on the Q4 beat, a $55M tariff refund, and the mid-June e.l.f. Hair category launch. The tension: FY2027 adjusted-EPS guidance of $3.27-$3.32 came in well below the ~$3.61 consensus, GAAP net income fell 77% to $26.3M (GAAP EPS $0.45 vs adjusted $3.13 - a very wide gap from Rhode deal costs, amortization, and SBC), and total debt jumped to $841.7M against $289.7M cash. This is a momentum re-rating on a decelerating-guide, newly levered story.
catalysts: Q1 FY2027 earnings on 2026-08-05: first full quarter showing whether the +12-14% guided growth is conservative or honest
Rhode international expansion into Mexico and seven European markets during FY2027
e.l.f. Hair launch (mid-June 2026): six mass-priced haircare SKUs via TikTok Shop, D2C, and Target online ahead of wider store rollout - a whole new category if it works
Further tariff relief following the $55M tariff refund received in mid-2026
Continued market-share gains across all five brands (management-cited momentum at Q4)
risk_factors: FY2027 adjusted EPS guidance $3.27-$3.32 vs ~$3.61 consensus - the Street reset targets downward (one prominent reset from $85 to $50) even as the stock rallied
GAAP/adjusted gap: FY2026 GAAP EPS $0.45 vs adjusted $3.13; GAAP net income -77% to $26.3M - quality of earnings depends heavily on add-backs
Leverage: total debt $841.7M (from $256.7M) vs $289.7M cash after the Rhode acquisition - net debt ~$552M on a company with $26.3M GAAP net income
Momentum/beta risk: beta 2.39 and a +47% June move mean the position re-prices violently on any guide-down; the 5-day +21% into the pass1 snapshot is sentiment, not new fundamentals
Category/fad risk: mass cosmetics and TikTok-driven brands (Rhode ~80% growth) have short fashion cycles; core e.l.f. growth is decelerating (guided +12-14% vs +25% delivered)
No free-cash-flow figure was verifiable in this pass - valuation must proxy owner earnings from adjusted EPS with an explicit haircut
